# FR-1: Game Initialization

## Description

The game must initialize with the player docked at a station, equipped with 100 credits and a small cargo hold, and be immediately playable after installation.

## Functional Requirements

- FR-1.1: The game must start with the player positioned at a station
- FR-1.2: The player must begin with exactly 100 credits
- FR-1.3: The player must start with a small cargo hold capacity
- FR-1.4: The game must be playable immediately after `npm install && npm start` without any manual build steps
- FR-1.5: The game must display the station interface upon initial load

## Rationale

This requirement ensures a consistent starting experience for all players and establishes the initial game state that enables the core gameplay loop of trading and exploration.

## Acceptance Criteria

- When the game loads, the player is automatically docked at a station
- The player's credit balance is initialized to 100
- The player has a working cargo hold with base capacity
- No additional configuration or build steps are required after installation
- The station interface is immediately accessible and functional

---

# FR-2: Space System Navigation

## Description

The game must provide at least 8 named star systems with stations that the player can navigate between using hyperspace jump mechanics.

## Functional Requirements

- FR-2.1: The game must include at least 8 distinct star systems
- FR-2.2: Each star system must have a unique name
- FR-2.3: Each star system must contain at least one station
- FR-2.4: The player must be able to view and select destination systems from a navigation interface
- FR-2.5: Hyperspace jumps must consume fuel from the player's ship
- FR-2.6: Each hyperspace jump must carry a probability of pirate encounter
- FR-2.7: The player must be able to initiate a hyperspace jump to a selected system

## Rationale

Space exploration is a core gameplay element, providing the environment for trading, combat, and progression. Multiple systems with dynamic pricing create meaningful travel decisions and economic opportunities.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A navigation screen displays all available star systems with their names
- Selecting a system shows jump requirements (fuel cost, distance, etc.)
- Initiating a jump consumes the specified amount of fuel
- After jumping, the player arrives in the selected system and can dock at its station
- Pirate encounters occur based on the defined probability during jumps
- The player cannot jump if insufficient fuel is available

---

# FR-3: Commodity Trading System

## Description

The game must implement a commodity market with dynamic per-system pricing that allows players to buy low and sell high across different star systems.

## Functional Requirements

- FR-3.1: The game must support trading of multiple commodity types
- FR-3.2: Each station must offer commodities for purchase
- FR-3.3: Each station must buy commodities from the player
- FR-3.4: Commodity prices must vary between different star systems
- FR-3.5: The player must have a cargo hold capacity that limits commodity quantities
- FR-3.6: The player must be able to view current commodity prices at each station
- FR-3.7: The player must be able to buy commodities if sufficient credits and cargo space are available
- FR-3.8: The player must be able to sell commodities if the cargo contains them
- FR-3.9: Transactions must update the player's credits and cargo accordingly

## Rationale

Trading is the primary economic loop of the game. Dynamic pricing across systems creates profitable trade routes and encourages exploration, while cargo capacity limits create strategic decisions about what to carry.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A market screen shows available commodities with buy/sell prices
- Players can select commodities to buy or sell with quantity selection
- The system prevents purchases when credits are insufficient
- The system prevents purchases when cargo capacity is exceeded
- The system prevents sales when the player doesn't own the commodity
- Price differences between systems create profitable trading opportunities
- All transactions correctly update credits and cargo inventory

# FR-4: Ship Combat System

## Description

The game must provide ship-to-ship combat with player lasers against enemy AI, allowing players to win combat or flee.

## Functional Requirements

- FR-4.1: The game must spawn enemy ships during pirate encounters
- FR-4.2: The player ship must be equipped with laser weapons
- FR-4.3: Enemy ships must have AI behavior for combat
- FR-4.4: Combat must occur in real-time with player control
- FR-4.5: The player must be able to fire lasers at enemy ships
- FR-4.6: Enemy ships must be able to damage the player's ship
- FR-4.7: The player must be able to attempt to flee from combat
- FR-4.8: Victory in combat must reward the player
- FR-4.9: Defeat in combat must have consequences for the player

## Rationale

Combat provides excitement and risk to the gameplay, creating tension during travel and additional progression paths through combat rewards. The option to flee adds strategic depth to encounters.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Combat initiates when a pirate encounter occurs
- The player can control ship movement and fire lasers
- Enemy AI pursues and attacks the player
- Lasers deal damage to shields and hull
- The player can attempt to disengage and flee
- Winning combat grants rewards (credits, cargo, or progression)
- Losing combat results in ship damage or death with appropriate consequences
- Combat includes visual effects for lasers and impacts

# FR-5: Ship Upgrade System

## Description

The game must allow players to purchase ship upgrades for cargo capacity, laser, shields, and fuel tank using credits earned through gameplay.

## Functional Requirements

- FR-5.1: The game must offer upgradeable ship modules: cargo capacity, laser, shields, fuel tank
- FR-5.2: Each upgrade type must have multiple levels or tiers
- FR-5.3: Each upgrade must have a credit cost
- FR-5.4: Upgrades must enhance the corresponding ship capability
- FR-5.5: The player must be able to view available upgrades and their costs
- FR-5.6: The player must be able to purchase upgrades if credits are sufficient
- FR-5.7: Purchased upgrades must immediately affect ship performance
- FR-5.8: The upgrade system must track current upgrade levels

## Rationale

Ship upgrades provide a progression system that rewards successful trading and combat, giving players long-term goals and customizing their playstyle. Upgrades create meaningful economic decisions about how to spend credits.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An upgrade screen displays all available modules with current levels and costs
- Players can select and purchase upgrades if they have sufficient credits
- Cargo upgrades increase maximum cargo capacity
- Laser upgrades increase weapon damage or fire rate
- Shield upgrades increase shield capacity or regeneration
- Fuel tank upgrades increase maximum fuel capacity
- Upgrades take effect immediately upon purchase
- The system correctly deducts credits and updates ship stats

# FR-6: Save/Load Game State

## Description

The game must provide functionality to save and load the complete game state, preserving player progress across sessions.

## Functional Requirements

- FR-6.1: The game must allow players to save their current game state
- FR-6.2: The game must allow players to load a previously saved game state
- FR-6.3: Save files must preserve all player progress (credits, cargo, upgrades, location)
- FR-6.4: Save files must preserve ship status (shields, fuel, hull)
- FR-6.5: Save files must preserve game progression (Elite rating, combat kills)
- FR-6.6: The save/load system must use local filesystem access
- FR-6.7: The game must provide UI for initiating save and load operations
- FR-6.8: The system must handle save/load errors gracefully

## Rationale

Save/load functionality is essential for a game of this scope, allowing players to progress over multiple sessions and protect their investment of time. Local storage keeps the game offline and self-contained.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Players can save their game through a clearly accessible UI option
- Players can load saved games through a clearly accessible UI option
- Loading a game restores the exact state at the time of saving
- All player stats, ship configuration, and progress are preserved
- The system handles file permission errors and missing save files appropriately
- Save files are stored in a predictable location on the local filesystem

# FR-7: Elite Rating Progression

## Description

The game must track player progress toward the Elite rating based on accumulated profit and combat kills.

## Functional Requirements

- FR-7.1: The game must track the player's total accumulated profit from trading
- FR-7.2: The game must track the player's total combat kills
- FR-7.3: The game must calculate an Elite rating based on profit and kills
- FR-7.4: The Elite rating must have multiple tiers or levels
- FR-7.5: The player must be able to view their current Elite rating
- FR-7.6: The progression system must persist across game sessions
- FR-7.7: The rating must increase as the player achieves more profit and kills

## Rationale

The Elite rating provides a long-term progression goal that rewards both trading and combat playstyles, giving players a sense of achievement and measuring their overall success in the game.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A status screen displays the player's current Elite rating
- The rating reflects both trading profit and combat accomplishments
- The rating increases as the player earns more profit and kills
- Progress is correctly saved and loaded with the game state
- The rating system provides clear milestones or tiers for players to achieve

---

# FR-8: Visual Rendering System

## Description

The game must provide a canvas/WebGL rendering system with parallax starfield, hyperspace jump effects, station docking screens, ship HUD, and combat visual effects.

## Functional Requirements

- FR-8.1: The game must render a parallax starfield background
- FR-8.2: The game must render visual effects for hyperspace jumps
- FR-8.3: The game must render station docking screens
- FR-8.4: The game must render a ship HUD displaying shields, fuel, cargo, and credits
- FR-8.5: The game must render visual effects for combat (lasers, explosions)
- FR-8.6: The rendering system must achieve 60fps on target hardware
- FR-8.7: The game must use canvas or WebGL for rendering
- FR-8.8: Visual elements must be clearly visible and readable

## Rationale

High-quality visuals are essential for game immersion and the "first-class acceptance subject" requirement. The rendering system must be performant enough to maintain smooth gameplay while delivering the visual experience described in the initiative.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The starfield background provides depth through parallax scrolling
- Hyperspace jumps have distinctive visual effects that convey speed and distance
- Station screens are visually distinct and provide clear station information
- The ship HUD clearly displays all relevant status information
- Combat effects provide clear feedback for hits, damage, and explosions
- The frame rate remains at or near 60fps during normal gameplay on target hardware
- All visual elements are rendered without artifacts or glitches

# FR-9: Server and Health Endpoint

## Description

The Node.js server must serve the game frontend and expose a /healthz endpoint for system status checks.

## Functional Requirements

- FR-9.1: The server must serve the single HTML/JS frontend
- FR-9.2: The server must expose a /healthz endpoint
- FR-9.3: The /healthz endpoint must return a success status when the server is running
- FR-9.4: The server must start when `npm start` is executed
- FR-9.5: The server must handle static file requests for the game
- FR-9.6: The server must be configurable for the port number

## Rationale

The server component is required for serving the game locally and providing a health check endpoint for operational monitoring. This ensures the game can be properly deployed and monitored.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Running `npm start` launches the server on the configured port
- Accessing the server root serves the game frontend
- Accessing /healthz returns a 200 OK status with appropriate response
- The server handles all static file requests for the game
- The server can be configured to run on different ports
- The server logs appropriate startup and error messages
